plastron appendicitis: No prior abdominal surgeries or systemic disease
Denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weight loss, night sweats, diarrhea, or constipation
Chief complaint: abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant
Abdominal examination showed voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant and minimal tenderness elsewhere
Ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis

Computed tomography of the abdomen revealed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant, causing partial luminal obliteration and edema on the anterolateral aspect of the cecum
